'''Eva Viehmann''' (born 1980)  is a German mathematician who holds a professorial chair in the arithmetic geometry and representation theory research group at the [[University of Münster]].{{r|i135}} Before that she was a professor working on [[arithmetic geometry]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]].{{r|tum}}

Viehmann studied at the [[University of Bonn]], where her 2005 doctoral thesis, ''On affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties for <math>\operatorname{GL}_n</math>'' (supervised by [[Michael Rapoport]]){{r|mgp}} won the Felix Hausdorff Memorial Award. She earned her [[habilitation]] in 2010, and in 2012 was appointed to her professorship at the Technical University of Munich.{{r|kaven}}

Viehmann won the 2012 von Kaven Award in mathematics of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] for her work on the [[Langlands program]].{{r|kaven}}
She was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on Lie Theory and Generalizations.{{r|icm}}
She was also the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2018.{{r|dmvpa}} In 2021 she became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].{{r|leo}}
